step: evaluator smoke, third evaluation (after the builder's reliability fixes)
rerun_note: No re-run: neither run crashed or raised a run-level error (exit code 0, trace error=null), so the one-time re-run allowance was not used. Both runs are DEGRADED (placeholder report only).
stop_rule_note: Brief: stop if the first run immediately fails with a Groq daily token limit (TPD) error for every section. The first run did not match: the trace records only the short reason 'RateLimitError 429' and does not say whether Groq's limit was per-minute or per-day; Groq answered 4 calls successfully, Gemini 2; and Gemini (the first provider) also returned 429. So the stop rule was not shown to apply and the second topic was run once. Whether the limit was TPD is not measured.
sample_size_note: n=1 per topic per evaluation. Smoke test, not a benchmark: no means, no significance, no generalisation.
third_evaluation_note: Ran after the builder's reliability fixes (verified by the builder only with fakes): Groq gpt-oss default temperature / reasoning_effort low / include_reasoning false / more token headroom; empty replies counted as retryable errors (trace.llm.empty_replies) with per-provider failure reasons; fetch retries 403/429 once with browser-like headers; workers keep untried search-result URLs and a retry starts with a seeded fetch; critic reads up to 2,000 chars per source; claims the critic names without quoted evidence are kept under 'Unverified claims'. Code differs from the first two evaluations, and the runs are single and rate-limited, so nothing here is a controlled comparison.
command: uv run reporter multi --out examples/multi/<topic>.md "<topic>" (default flags and budgets; critic and writer on); run sequentially, small-language-models first, then carbon-capture
quota_check: CLI only, as instructed; no manual API calls. No separate check was possible beyond the first run itself.
full_report_saved: none: neither run produced a report. examples/multi/ holds the two placeholder files ('No report could be written' plus coverage notes). The second evaluation's reports are preserved in examples/multi_second_run/.

gemini_finding.small_language_models_run: Gemini: 58 calls recorded, 56 failed (all 'RateLimitError 429'), 2 succeeded. The 2 successes were the supervisor plan calls at the start (model gemini-3.6-flash); the plan was then rejected ('plan_generic: no valid section from the supervisor') and a generic 3-section plan was used. After that Gemini returned 429 on every call, so Groq handled the rest.
gemini_finding.carbon_capture_run: Gemini: 84 calls recorded, 84 failed (all 'RateLimitError 429'), 0 succeeded. Groq took every successful call (12).
gemini_finding.why_it_failed: Provider rate limit (HTTP 429) on 140 of 142 Gemini calls over the two runs. The trace stores only the short reason 'RateLimitError 429'; it does not say which Gemini limit (per minute, per day, or quota exhausted) was hit. That is not measured.
gemini_finding.answer: Gemini WAS in the chain (first), it was tried on every call, and it failed almost entirely on 429 rate limits (2 of 142 calls succeeded, both plan calls in the first run). Gemini therefore did not rescue the Groq failures. This closes the earlier 'Gemini never used, no reason in the trace' gap: it was used, and the reason is a 429.
gemini_finding.secrets_note: provider names only; .env was not read or printed

groq_finding.tpd_or_tpm: not measured (reason stored without the limit type)
groq_finding.possible_context_not_verified: The second evaluation recorded Groq's daily token limit (200000, ~198.7k used) at about 17:20 UTC on 2026-10-30; this evaluation started at 23:33 UTC the same day. A rolling daily window would plausibly not have reset, but this was not checked.

retry_evidence_summary.answer: The retry fired for 3 of 3 sections in each run (6 of 6), but 0 of 6 improved in verdict (all fail -> fail) and 0 of 6 gained a finding. Pages rose in 1 of 6 (small-language-models s3, 0 -> 1, kept the retry), stayed the same in 4 and fell in 1 (carbon-capture s1, 1 -> 0). The critic's LLM review did not run in either run (no finding existed), so every verdict is deterministic.
retry_evidence_summary.did_retry_improve: no (verdict-level: 0 of 6). Whether a retry helps when the LLM calls succeed is not measured here.

reliability_fixes_effect.empty_replies: Router now counts them: 34 (small-language-models run) and 8 (carbon-capture run) provider calls returned no text. The note-based counts that were 9 and 27 in the second evaluation's SLM run are 0 here only because the path moved into the router; counts are not comparable across metrics. Rate of empty replies among Groq calls: 34/48 and 8/64 (not an improvement that can be claimed; the second evaluation did not record a Groq call total).
reliability_fixes_effect.fetch: Fetch layer, counting model-issued fetches plus seeded candidate fetches: 10 ok, 2 failed of 12 attempts (small-language-models run: 4 ok, 0 failed; carbon-capture run: 6 ok, 2 failed). The 2 failures were both in the carbon-capture run: 1 HTTP 403 after both tries (mdpi.com) and 1 timeout at 10.086 s (osti.gov). All 6 seeded candidate fetches succeeded (2 + 4). Whether the 403 header retry ever succeeded is not measured; 1 URL still ended in 403 after both tries. No PDF fetch occurred.
reliability_fixes_effect.llm_availability: Not fixed. Gemini: 142 calls over the two runs, 140 failed on 429, 2 succeeded. Groq: 112 calls, 16 succeeded, 42 empty replies, 54 rate-limit 429. Across both runs no worker produced a finding (findings 0 -> 0 in all 6 retries).
reliability_fixes_effect.failure_picture_changed: Yes in kind, no in outcome. In kind: pages are now fetched (5 of 6 sections had at least one fetched page: 2 of 3 in the small-language-models run, 3 of 3 in the carbon-capture run) and failures are visible per provider. In outcome: still 0 reports, 0 sections with a usable finding, 0 critic passes. The blocker moved from the fetch layer (second evaluation: 0 pages in 3 sections) to LLM availability (Gemini 429, Groq 429/empty).

smoke_comparison.caveat: n=1 per system per topic. Units differ (R0 questions covered of 5; R1 sections complete of 5; R2 sections with a fetched page, with critic pass count). The third R2 evaluation planned only 3 sections per topic (generic fallback in one run), so its 'of 3' is not comparable with 'of 5'. Runs differ in code version and in provider quota state. The third evaluation's tokens are low because most LLM calls failed (calls without token counts: 9 and 8) and failed calls carry no token count. No means, no significance.
